# `quadrature`

the quadrature spectrum of the sources per band (the quadrature fraction, the energy per source, the strongest quadrature pairs).

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run quadrature --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run quadrature --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run quadrature --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --kernel KERNEL [--bands '[{name: alpha, lo: 8, hi: 12}]'] [--pairs 3]
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `kernel` | operator inverse kernel, from recording.manifold.0, where {"name": "$kernel"} | yes |
| `bad` | selection spans, manifold recording.time, where {"name": "{recording}_bad_segments"}, required false | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `kernel` | `--kernel` | `none` | - |  | the inverse kernel's name (free or fixed orientation), or none: the subject's one inverse kernel on the recording's channels |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording}_{kernel}_quadrature` | - |  | the stem of the stored statistics: <name> (the pairs) and <name>_energy; their segment partition <name>_segments |
| `bands` | `--bands` | `[{"name": "delta", "lo": 2, "hi": 4}, {"name": "theta", "lo": 5, "hi": 7}, {"name": "alpha", "lo": 8, "hi": 12}, {"name": "beta", "lo": 15, "hi": 29}, {"name": "gamma1", "lo": 30, "hi": 59}, {"name": "gamma2", "lo": 60, "hi": 90}]` | Hz |  | the bands: {name, lo, hi}; a band holds the bins from lo to hi inclusive (Brainstorm's default bands) |
| `pairs` | `--pairs` | `3` | - |  | the k strongest quadrature pairs per band |
| `segment_seconds` | `--segment-seconds` | `4.0` | s |  | the segment's length in seconds (under segment_rule tile it snaps to the nearest 2^k samples) |
| `segment_samples` | `--segment-samples` | none | samples |  | the segment's length in samples (wins over segment_seconds); null: from segment_seconds |
| `segment_rule` | `--segment-rule` | `tile` | - | tile, round, even | how the segment's length becomes samples: tile \| round \| even |
| `overlap` | `--overlap` | `0.5` | fraction |  | the fraction of a segment shared with the next, in [0, 1) |
| `window` | `--window` | `hamming` | - | hann, hamming, blackman, rectangular | the taper of each segment |
| `periodic` | `--periodic` | false | - |  | the DFT-even form of the window rather than the symmetric one |
| `detrend` | `--detrend` | `constant` | - | none, constant, linear | what is removed from each segment before windowing |
| `scaling` | `--scaling` | `density` | - | density, spectrum, chain | density = power per Hz \| spectrum = power \| chain = per sample, per bin |
| `bad_segments` | `--bad-segments` | `exclude` | - | exclude, ignore | exclude = a segment touching one of the recording's bad segments is left out \| ignore = every segment is kept |

## Presets

`--set <preset>` sets the parameters below at once; a parameter given by name wins over the preset.

| preset | sets |
|---|---|
| `tiles` | segment_rule=tile |
| `brainstorm` | segment_rule=round, window=hamming, periodic=false, detrend=constant, scaling=density |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.xpsd`](../nodes.md) | x=recording, channels_of=kernel, exclude=bad | bands=$bands, segment_seconds=$segment_seconds, segment_samples=$segment_samples, segment_rule=$segment_rule, overlap=$overlap, window=$window, periodic=$periodic, detrend=$detrend, scaling=$scaling, bad_segments=$bad_segments | channels, spectrum, bins |
| after | [`signal.source_planes`](../nodes.md) | spectrum=spectrum, kernel=kernel | pairs=$pairs | energy, pairs |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `energy` | kind statistic, name $name_energy, of recording, axes [{"name": "vertex", "on": "kernel.to"}, {"name": "band"}], partition {"tiling": "$name_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |
| `pairs` | kind statistic, name $name, of recording, axes [{"name": "vertex", "on": "kernel.to"}, {"name": "pattern"}], partition {"tiling": "$name_segments", "on": "recording.time"} |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE QUADRATURE SPECTRUM OF A RECORDING'S SOURCES (two statistics): what no zero-delay mixing can make of the sources' band cross-spectrum. The sensors' band cross-spectrum (Welch, streamed
chunk by chunk, the recording's bad segments left out, on the kernel's channels), its factor L (S = L L^H), and F = K L through the kernel (never an N x N matrix); from F, per band, the
quadrature fraction ||Im C||_F / ||C||_F (0 for any zero-delay mixture), the quadrature energy of each source (sum over the others of (Im C)^2; a free kernel's three rows added) and the strongest
pairs of Im C: p leads q by a quarter cycle, the pattern turns p -> q. A free kernel reads the quadrature over its 3N rows; a pair is one pattern over them, stored as its x y z components.
The kernel spreads each source over its neighbours with no lag: it shrinks Im C, so a quadrature fraction is a lower bound of what the sources hold.

THE GRAPH. recording --[signal.xpsd, accumulate: partition = the Welch segments (a Rule on the time line)]--> spectrum --[signal.source_planes, array: pointwise matrix maths with the
kernel, no neighbourhood]--> energy, pairs. Reductions over time are the cross-spectrum's (a statistic over the segment partition); the per-source values are one member each.
Stored: the statistics `<name>_energy` (vertex x band) and `<name>` (vertex x pattern: `pair<k>_<p|q>_<band>`), their segment partition `<name>_segments`.

  nxr-neuro run quadrature --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --kernel KERNEL [--bands '[{name: alpha, lo: 8, hi: 12}]'] [--pairs 3]
```
